q: Should I drop peterson for derozan?
short: No. Keep Darryn Peterson: he has 4 games this week to DeRozan's 3, and DeRozan's 15.6 FP per game this season is far below his 29.8 projection.
answer:
Peterson projects at 29.1 FP per game and has averaged 33.8 over 14 games this season. He has 4 games left this week (Nov 17, 18, 20, 22), worth about 126.9 projected FP.

DeRozan projects at 29.8 per game, only 0.7 more than Peterson, and he has just 3 games this week, so he would add roughly 89 FP. That projection also looks generous: he is averaging 15.6 FP over 11 games this season on 22.7 minutes. Swapping would cost you about 38 FP this week for a tiny per-game gain that the actual production does not support.

Your roster is full, with 15 active players plus Edwards and Morant on your 2 IR spots, so any add needs a drop. If you want to pick up DeRozan anyway, drop a bench player instead. He is a free agent, so the add is instant. Peterson is also a young high-usage guard whose scoring gives you more upside than DeRozan.

I did not search the web for news, since this is a pure value comparison from your league data.

moves.do: Keep Darryn Peterson and do not add DeMar DeRozan
moves.why: Peterson has 4 games and about 126.9 projected FP this week against about 89 for DeRozan's 3 games, and DeRozan is only at 15.6 FP per game this season.
